newsitem.title: JORDAN: Palestinian firm expands despite political worries.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian firm expands despite political worries.

text.p: Palestine Development and Investment Company (Padico) said on Monday it was proceeding with multi-million dollar projects despite uncertainty over Middle East peace.
"We are determined to proceed with plans we have begun whatever hesitancy there is by some investors," said Sabih Masri, a major Padico shareholder.

He said the company hoped it could overcome investor uncertainty after the election of a right-wing Israeli government in May. The company still aimed to implement $1 billion of projects in Palestinian self-rule areas by 2000.
"Our group is continuing... despite the delay because of Israeli practices and obstacles," he said.
The Amman-based Padico, a Liberian-registered holding company with $152 million paid-up capital, held its second annual meeting on Monday.

It is by far the largest Palestinian private sector company, set up amid peace euphoria after 1993 to mobilise the financial clout and expertise of expatriate Palestinians for business ventures in Gaza and the West Bank.

It showed a net profit of $233,596 in 1995 against $67,879 in its first year, with much of its capital consumed in start-up costs and the founding of six subsidiaries in which Padico has stakes of between 18 and 49 percent.

Padico blames a difficult investment climate on stalled Israeli-Palestinian peace talks and on Israeli obstacles to free flow of goods and labour to self-rule areas, which it said was choking the nascent Palestinian economy.

Shareholders reviewed Padico's six main subsidiaries, and its plans for a $60 million Gaza industrial park, and a telecommunications firm in which Palestinian self-rule authorities have taken an eight percent stake.

Construction work on the Gaza Industrial Estate which will be partly funded by the World Bank and USAID would be completed by end of 1997, with plans for another in Nablus, said Kamal al-Shaer, the company chairman.

General manager Hatem Halawani said the Palestine Telecommunications Company (Paltel) will invest $200 million over the next three years to add 250,000 lines. A GSM mobile system will add 120,000 lines in five years at a cost of $50 million.

Paltel, in which Padico has an 18 percent stake, signed an accord with the Palestinian Authority last November granting it an exclusive concession to rehabilitate and expand the existing run-down telephone system in self-rule Gaza and the West Bank.

Shaer said the automated $2 million Palestine Securities Exchange (PSE), in which PADICO has a 70 percent stake, was due to start trading in Nablus in January with 60 listed companies with a total market capitalisation of above $500 million.
Padico has installed a dealing system, supplied by Canadian firm EFA, at the bourse's offices overlooking Nablus, the designated ecomomic capital of self-rule areas.

A $25 million capital Palestine Tourism Investment Company, in which Padico also has a stake, is being formed, with plans to build a $40 million five-star hotel and commercial complex in Bethlehem to be opened by 1999.

Nabil Sarraf, chairman of the Palestine Real Estate Company, 49 percent owned by Padico, is proceeding with a $200 million housing project, the biggest yet in Gaza, together with another $40 million project begun recently.
